item.title: [ 70] The blame lies with whoever made the trailer
item.description:
>Geoff overhyped it
Geoff gave them a premium ad slot for free. Without his intervention the game would have been forgotten by the end of the showcase. It's not his fault they squandered the attention. People hated the game before they had even played it. That's not mismanaged expectations, that's a horrible first impression.

>hero shooters are oversaturated
Bullshit. Marvel Rivals, Arc Raiders, and Deadlock are all recent, genre-adjacent games that are popular. I'd estimate there's room for one new live-service title every half-year at least. Holding those numbers long-term is where things get tricky, but Highguard flopped immediately so that's not even relevant.

>the game is bad
It's not good enough to save bad marketing, but it's not awful. You're kidding yourself if you believe the "Mostly Negative" Steam rating is anything but review bombing for the memes. If this game were reskinned after a more popular IP, I doubt it would get nitpicked as much.

>THE REAL PROBLEM
The blame lies with a bad trailer/promo from a marketing department that's at least 10 years out of date. They're the ones who chose to feature the mushroom haircut guy as the franchise icon because they thought zoomers would find him relatable. They're the ones who decided to show a bunch of action shots of hero abilities seemingly unaware that stuff is literally the least distinctive thing about their game. Compare to Divinity who did a simple teaser that told a story about the setting. I can't say that Highguard would have been a success with something more like that, but it wouldn't have become an instant punchline.

item.title: [ 59] Eighth District Rules in Favor of ICE
item.description:
> Thread theme: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Qp_SrTgBBs

> https://katv.com/news/nation-world/federal-eighth-circuit-appellate-court-blocks-lower-district-judges-restrictions-on-minnesota-immigration-law-enforcement-operations

HUNT VALLEY, Md. (TNND) — A federal appellate court blocked a lower judge's restrictions on immigration law enforcement’s Minnesota operations on Monday.

A three-judge panel in the 8th Circuit, which has an office in Saint Paul, stayed District Judge Katherine Menendez’s order that prohibited federal agents from retaliating or using pepper spray against protesters. Menendez also blocked officers from stopping protesters who are following their activities in their cars.

“The district court entered a preliminary injunction with respect to federal immigration-enforcement operations in Minnesota. The injunction is unlikely to survive the government’s interlocutory appeal, ... so we stay it pending a final decision in this case,” the panel, which includes Judges Raymond Gruender, Bobby Shepherd and David Stras, wrote.

The bench ruled that Menendez’s order is too vague. Her direction for law enforcement to not retaliate against people “engaging in peaceful and unobstructive protest activity,” as well as the judge’s prohibition on “stopping or detaining drivers ... where there is no reasonable articulable suspicion that they are forcibly obstructing or interfering with" agents, are simply commands to “obey the law,” according to the appellate court.

“Even the provision that singles out the use of ‘pepper-spray or similar nonlethal munitions and crowd dispersal tools’ requires federal agents to predict what the district court would consider ‘peaceful and unobstructive protest activity,’” the panel said.

De-botnet your life. Learn something new. Serving applications to yourself, your family, and your frens feels good. Put your tech skills to good use for yourself and those close to you. But seriously what the fuck, do people who do this shit only stick to one climate year-round or something? Am I doing something wrong or are all these /one bag/ or carry on only fags simply just not spending much time traveling.
